finding.claim: Checkout of an untrusted tree can write files outside the worktree on case-insensitive filesystems (default on macOS and Windows). A symlink entry 'A' pointing at an existing external directory is created first, then a blob at 'a/authorized_keys' is written through it, because parent path components are never checked for symlinks.
finding.source: Remote tree entries (attacker-controlled repository content) during clone/checkout: entry 'A' with mode 120000 and an absolute target, and tree 'a' containing blob 'authorized_keys'.
finding.sink: open(target_path, 'wb') at dulwich/index.py:1916 (via os.makedirs at index.py:2231-2232 and build_file_from_blob at index.py:2246).

trace.note: clone/checkout calls build_index_from_tree
iter_tree_contents yields entries in name order (object_store.py:3775 iteritems(name_order=True)), so 'A' (0x41) is processed before 'a/...'
validate_path checks each element by name only
full_path built from root plus entry path, with no realpath or lstat of parent components
os.path.exists(dirname) resolves through the 'A' symlink on a case-insensitive FS, so makedirs is skipped
only a symlink at the final path component is removed before writing
open(target,'wb') follows the parent symlink and writes outside the worktree

finding.guards_checked: (1) validate_path_element: default/NTFS/HFS validators only reject .git, ., .., empty, and NTFS/HFS spellings; they do not reject case-folded collisions or symlinked parents (index.py:2019-2168). (2) Final-component symlink replacement at index.py:1904-1910 covers only the leaf. (3) No realpath/containment check against the worktree root anywhere in build_index_from_tree. Not executed: the symlink-parent case was verified by code reading only; the scratch repro could not run.
finding.repro: Tree with entries 'A' (symlink -> existing external dir, e.g. /Users/victim/.ssh) and 'a/' (dir containing authorized_keys). Run build_index_from_tree on a case-insensitive FS. Expected: authorized_keys is written into the external directory.

finding.claim: Ref names with empty components (e.g. refs/heads//main) pass validation via a deprecation shim. The update hook sees the non-canonical name, but the write lands on the same file as refs/heads/main. A server update hook that guards protected branches by exact name can be bypassed.
finding.source: Pushed ref name in the receive-pack command line (server.py:1747-1748).
finding.sink: Ref write in the refs container (refs.py:958 os.path.join(root_dir, path)) reached from set_if_equals/remove_if_equals (server.py:1593, 1588); the policy check is the update hook (server.py:1665-1678).

trace.note: client ref line parsed; ref name taken verbatim
_on_update invoked with the raw ref name
_check_refname
b'//' in name and collapsed form valid -> returns with only a DeprecationWarning
os.path.join collapses the double slash, so the file written is refs/heads/main
set_if_equals writes the ref

finding.guards_checked: check_ref_format (refs.py:118-154) passes on the collapsed name; compare-and-swap via old sha is intact; the update hook is the only policy control and it is optional (server.py:1678-1680, returns None when no hook). Not verified end-to-end through DiskRefsContainer's set path.
finding.repro: Configure hooks['update'] to deny exact name refs/heads/main. Push to refs/heads//main with the correct old sha. Expected: the hook does not match, and refs/heads/main is updated.

finding.claim: GunzipFilter decompresses Content-Encoding: gzip request bodies with no decompressed-size limit. LimitedInputFilter caps only the compressed Content-Length, so a small gzip bomb can drive unbounded memory or CPU use on the server.
finding.source: HTTP POST body with Content-Encoding: gzip to /git-upload-pack or /git-receive-pack (unauthenticated by default).
finding.sink: gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=environ['wsgi.input']) at web.py:765, read by the service handler (web.py:564-566).

trace.note: make_wsgi_chain: LimitedInputFilter(GunzipFilter(app))
LimitedInputFilter bounds the compressed bytes only
GunzipFilter wraps input in GzipFile with no output cap
handler reads decompressed stream
receive.maxInputSize defaults to 0 (unlimited), applying only to receive-pack

finding.guards_checked: Content-Length cap on the compressed stream; receive.maxInputSize (default unlimited, matches git); no decompressed-size cap in web.py or upload-pack. Severity: DoS only.
finding.repro: POST a ~1 MB gzip body that inflates to several GB with Content-Encoding: gzip to /git-upload-pack. Expected: unbounded memory growth.

finding.claim: apply_delta does not bound cumulative output against the declared dest_size while building the result. A small delta with many copy opcodes referencing a large base can allocate far more memory than the input size, which is a delta-bomb DoS.
finding.source: Pack data or a delta object from a remote fetch or push (untrusted pack).
finding.sink: out.append(src_buf[cp_off:cp_off+cp_size]) at pack.py:3869 with dest_size checked only at the end (pack.py:3879).

trace.note: dest_size taken from the delta header, not capped
per-op check: cp_size <= dest_size only, not a running total
each copy materializes up to src_size bytes
total size checked only after all ops run

finding.guards_checked: Per-copy bounds (cp_off+cp_size <= src_size, cp_size <= dest_size); final dest_size equality; index/length checks. Missing: running output cap during the loop.
finding.repro: Base of 1 MB, delta with declared dest_size large and about 1M copy ops of 1 MB each. Expected: memory grows toward multi-GB before the final size check.

finding.claim: The LFS batch endpoint passes the unvalidated JSON oid to _object_exists, which opens the path objects/<oid[0:2]>/<oid[2:4]>/<oid>. This is a server-side file-existence oracle for arbitrary paths, and reflects the Host header into hrefs.
finding.source: JSON body of POST /objects/batch (oid field) and the Host header.

trace.note: oid taken from the parsed JSON body
_object_exists(oid) with no _is_valid_oid check (the check exists only on the GET/PUT/verify routes)
open(self._sha_path(oid)) succeeds or raises KeyError
os.path.join builds the path from the attacker string

finding.guards_checked: _is_valid_oid on handle_download/upload/verify (lfs_server.py:173,198,242). Not applied on the batch path. The server is documented as 'for testing'. Content is not returned, so this is an existence oracle only.
finding.repro: POST /objects/batch with operation=download and oid='../../../../etc/passwd'-style traversal. Expected: an existing file is reported as downloadable, a missing one as 404.

finding.claim: submodule_update clones the URL taken from the repository's .gitmodules without restricting transports. file:// or local-path URLs are accepted, unlike git's default protocol.file restriction for submodules, so a malicious repository can cause local repositories on the cloning machine to be copied into the submodule store.
finding.source: .gitmodules url in the attacker's repository, copied into config by submodule_init.
finding.sink: clone(url, submodule_git_dir, bare=True) at porcelain/submodule.py:221, reached after config.get(section,b'url') at line 202.

trace.note: submodule_init copies url from .gitmodules into config
url read from config
clone() with that URL, no scheme allowlist

finding.guards_checked: Submodule path validation (_check_submodule_path, submodule.py:90-110) covers the path only, not the URL. No protocol allowlist exists in the client (no protocol.allow equivalent found by grep). Severity low: needs the victim to run submodule_update/init on an attacker repo, and impact is local data copy.
finding.repro: Set .gitmodules url to file:///path/to/private-repo, then submodule_update(init=True). Expected: the private repository is cloned into .git/modules.
